title: Slack
content:
## Overview

Connect your Emergent app to Slack to send notifications, receive commands, and build interactive chat experiences. This integration enables your app to post messages to channels, respond to user interactions, and leverage Slack's rich messaging features.

Common use cases include deployment notifications, error alerts, approval workflows, and conversational interfaces for your application logic.

## Prerequisites

Before integrating Slack, ensure you have:

- A Slack workspace where you have permission to install apps
- An active Emergent project
- Administrative access to your Emergent app's environment variables

## Setting up a Slack app

<Steps>
<Step title="Create a new Slack app">
Navigate to [api.slack.com/apps](https://api.slack.com/apps) and click **Create New App**. Choose **From scratch**, provide an app name (e.g., "My Emergent App"), and select the workspace where you want to install it.
</Step>

<Step title="Configure OAuth & permissions">
In your app's settings, go to **OAuth & Permissions** in the sidebar. Scroll down to **Bot Token Scopes** and add the permissions your app needs:

- `chat:write` — post messages to channels
- `chat:write.public` — post to channels without joining
- `channels:read` — view basic channel info
- `groups:read` — view private channel info (if needed)
- `im:read` and `im:write` — send direct messages
- `commands` — handle slash commands (if applicable)

Add any additional scopes required by your specific integration.
</Step>

<Step title="Install the app to your workspace">
At the top of the **OAuth & Permissions** page, click **Install to Workspace**. Slack will prompt you to authorize the app. Once approved, you'll receive a **Bot User OAuth Token** starting with `xoxb-`. Copy this token — you'll need it in the next section.
</Step>

<Step title="Configure event subscriptions (optional)">
If your app needs to respond to Slack events (messages, reactions, button clicks), enable **Event Subscriptions** in the sidebar.

Set the **Request URL** to your Emergent app's webhook endpoint (e.g., `https://your-app.emergent.run/api/slack/events`). Slack will verify this URL with a challenge request.

Subscribe to the bot events you need, such as `message.channels`, `app_mention`, or `message.im`.
</Step>

<Step title="Set up slash commands (optional)">
To handle slash commands like `/deploy` or `/status`, go to **Slash Commands** and click **Create New Command**.

Provide the command name, request URL (e.g., `https://your-app.emergent.run/api/slack/command`), and a brief description. Save your changes.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Note>
Slack will only send events to publicly accessible URLs. If you're developing locally, use a tool like ngrok to create a temporary tunnel, or deploy your app to Emergent's hosted environment first.
</Note>

## Adding credentials to Emergent

Your Emergent app needs the Slack bot token and signing secret to authenticate requests.

<Steps>
<Step title="Copy your credentials">
From your Slack app settings:

- Copy the **Bot User OAuth Token** from **OAuth & Permissions** (`xoxb-...`)
- Copy the **Signing Secret** from **Basic Information** under **App Credentials**
</Step>

<Step title="Set environment variables">
In your Emergent project chat, describe the environment variables you need:

```
Add these environment variables:
SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=xoxb-your-token-here
SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET=your-signing-secret
```

The AI agents will securely store these as encrypted environment variables in your app.
</Step>

<Step title="Use the credentials in code">
Reference the environment variables in your application logic:

<CodeGroup>
```javascript Node.js
const { WebClient } = require('@slack/web-api');
const client = new WebClient(process.env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN);

await client.chat.postMessage({
  channel: '#general',
  text: 'Deployment successful! 🚀'
});
```

```python Python
from slack_sdk import WebClient
import os

client = WebClient(token=os.environ['SLACK_BOT_TOKEN'])
client.chat_postMessage(
    channel='#general',
    text='Deployment successful! 🚀'
)
```
</CodeGroup>
</Step>
</Steps>

## Common integration patterns

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="Notification workflows" icon="bell">
Send alerts when deployments complete, errors occur, or user actions require attention. Post rich messages with buttons and attachments.
</Card>

<Card title="Approval flows" icon="circle-check">
Request approvals via interactive messages. Users click buttons to approve or reject, triggering webhooks back to your app.
</Card>

<Card title="Command interfaces" icon="terminal">
Implement slash commands that execute app logic directly from Slack, such as triggering builds or querying status.
</Card>

<Card title="Event-driven automation" icon="zap">
Listen for Slack events (mentions, reactions, new messages) and respond programmatically or trigger workflows.
</Card>
</CardGroup>

## Verifying webhook requests

<Warning>
Always verify that incoming webhook requests are genuinely from Slack using the signing secret. This prevents unauthorized parties from sending fake events to your app.
</Warning>

Slack signs each request with a timestamp and HMAC signature. Use the official SDKs or implement verification manually:

<CodeGroup>
```javascript Node.js
const crypto = require('crypto');

function verifySlackRequest(req) {
  const signature = req.headers['x-slack-signature'];
  const timestamp = req.headers['x-slack-request-timestamp'];
  const body = JSON.stringify(req.body);
  
  const hmac = crypto.createHmac('sha256', process.env.SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET);
  const [version, hash] = signature.split('=');
  hmac.update(`${version}:${timestamp}:${body}`);
  
  return crypto.timingSafeEqual(
    Buffer.from(hash, 'hex'),
    hmac.digest()
  );
}
```

```python Python
import hmac
import hashlib

def verify_slack_request(request):
    signature = request.headers['X-Slack-Signature']
    timestamp = request.headers['X-Slack-Request-Timestamp']
    body = request.get_data(as_text=True)
    
    base = f"v0:{timestamp}:{body}"
    expected = 'v0=' + hmac.new(
        os.environ['SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET'].encode(),
        base.encode(),
        hashlib.sha256
    ).hexdigest()
    
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature)
```
</CodeGroup>

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Messages aren't appearing in channels">
Verify that your bot has been added to the target channel. Either invite the bot manually (`/invite @YourBot`) or use the `chat:write.public` scope to post without joining.

Check that the channel ID or name is correct. Channel IDs start with `C` for public channels and `G` for private channels.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Webhook URL verification fails">
Ensure your endpoint responds to Slack's challenge request immediately with the `challenge` parameter in the response body. Do not perform long operations during verification.

If using Emergent's serverless functions, confirm the endpoint is deployed and publicly accessible.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Events aren't triggering">
Confirm that **Event Subscriptions** is enabled and the correct bot events are subscribed. Check your app's event logs in the Slack API dashboard for delivery failures.

Verify your request URL is returning HTTP 200 within three seconds. Slack will disable your endpoint after repeated timeouts.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Interactive components don't work">
Enable **Interactivity & Shortcuts** in your app settings and provide a **Request URL** for interaction payloads. This is separate from the events URL.

Ensure your endpoint can parse `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` payloads and respond within three seconds to acknowledge the interaction.
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>
